children.text: T3: Dipole in a magnetic field

Two small balls of mass \(m\) each, with charges \(+q\) and \(-q\), are joined by a rigid massless rod of length \(d\). This dipole lies parallel to plane \(XY\) in a uniform magnetic field \(\mathbf B=B\hat{\mathbf z}\), perpendicular to the plane. Initially it points along \(+X\), has angular velocity \(\omega_0\) in the plane, and its centre of mass starts at the origin with velocity \(\mathbf v_0\) parallel to \(XY\). Consider the distinct scenarios below.

nodes.alt: Original dipole diagram: negative charge minus q of mass m at left, positive charge plus q of mass m at right, separation d on the X axis, Y upwards, initial velocity v0 and angular velocity omega0, and perpendicular magnetic field B.

children.text: a
Find \(\omega_0\) and the direction of \(\mathbf v_0\) so that the centre of mass moves at constant velocity \(\mathbf v=\mathbf v_0\).
b
For given \(\omega_0\), find the direction and magnitude of \(\mathbf v_0\) for circular centre-of-mass motion. Find radius \(R_c\) and centre coordinates \(x_c,y_c\). You need not prove uniqueness.
c
For \(\mathbf v_0=0\), find the minimum initial angular-speed magnitude \(\omega_{\min}\) needed to reverse the dipole orientation.
d
For \(\mathbf v_0=0\) and \(\omega_0=\omega_{\min}\), the centre-of-mass trajectory has an asymptote. Find its distance \(D\) from the origin.
Useful vector identity:
\[\mathbf a\times(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c)=\mathbf b(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c)-\mathbf c(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b).\]

statement.text:
T3: Dipole in a magnetic field
Two small balls of mass \(m\) each, with charges \(+q\) and \(-q\), are joined by a rigid massless rod of length \(d\). This dipole lies parallel to plane \(XY\) in a uniform magnetic field \(\mathbf B=B\hat{\mathbf z}\), perpendicular to the plane. Initially it points along \(+X\), has angular velocity \(\omega_0\) in the plane, and its centre of mass starts at the origin with velocity \(\mathbf v_0\) parallel to \(XY\). Consider the distinct scenarios below.

a
Find \(\omega_0\) and the direction of \(\mathbf v_0\) so that the centre of mass moves at constant velocity \(\mathbf v=\mathbf v_0\).
b
For given \(\omega_0\), find the direction and magnitude of \(\mathbf v_0\) for circular centre-of-mass motion. Find radius \(R_c\) and centre coordinates \(x_c,y_c\). You need not prove uniqueness.
c
For \(\mathbf v_0=0\), find the minimum initial angular-speed magnitude \(\omega_{\min}\) needed to reverse the dipole orientation.
d
For \(\mathbf v_0=0\) and \(\omega_0=\omega_{\min}\), the centre-of-mass trajectory has an asymptote. Find its distance \(D\) from the origin.
Useful vector identity:
\[\mathbf a\times(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c)=\mathbf b(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c)-\mathbf c(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b).\]

children.text: T3: Dipole in a magnetic field
a. Uniform translation
Let \(\mathbf r\) point from the centre to the positive charge, and \(\mathbf p=2q\mathbf r\). The charge velocities are \(\mathbf v_\pm=\mathbf v\pm\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r\), so
\[\mathbf F=q(\mathbf v_+-\mathbf v_-)\times\mathbf B=2q(\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r)\times\mathbf B=B\omega\mathbf p.\]

nodes.alt: Original diagram resolving each charge's velocity into the centre velocity and opposite rotational contributions, with r pointing to the positive charge and omega counterclockwise.

children.text: Constant centre velocity requires \(\omega=0\). The torque is \(\boldsymbol\tau=2q\mathbf r\times(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)=-2q\mathbf B(\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf v)\), so maintaining zero rotation also requires \(\mathbf v\perp\mathbf r\). Initially the dipole points along \(X\). Thus \(\omega_0=0\), and \(\mathbf v_0\) can point along either direction of \(Y\), with arbitrary speed. Zero velocity is also a stationary limiting case.
b. Circular orbit

For circular motion \(\mathbf F\) points towards the circle centre. Since \(\mathbf F\parallel\mathbf p\), the dipole remains radial and rotates with the orbital angular velocity \(\omega_0\). There is no torque because velocity is perpendicular to the rod. Centripetal balance gives \(2mv_0^2/R_c=pBv_0/R_c\). Therefore
\[\mathbf v_0=-\frac{qBd}{2m}\hat{\mathbf y},\qquad R_c=\frac{qBd}{2m|\omega_0|},\qquad (x_c,y_c)=\left(\frac{qBd}{2m\omega_0},0\right).\]

nodes.alt: Original circular-orbit construction: dipole radial towards the marked circle centre (xc,yc), charge velocities tangent to the orbit and net force directed towards the centre.

children.text: Here \(\omega_0\ne0\). Positive angular velocity places the centre on \(+X\), negative on \(-X\), while the initial velocity points downwards in both cases. The answer fields use \(w=|\omega_0|\) for radius, and signed \(\omega_0\) for \(x_c\).
c. Reversal threshold

Integrating \(2m\dot{\mathbf v}=\dot{\mathbf p}\times\mathbf B\) gives conserved generalized momentum \(2m\mathbf v-\mathbf p\times\mathbf B\). Starting from rest, reversal \(\mathbf p_1=-\mathbf p_0\) requires \(\mathbf v_1=-\mathbf p_0\times\mathbf B/m\), with speed \(qBd/m\). Magnetic forces do no work, so with \(I=md^2/2\),
\[\frac12 I\omega_0^2=\frac12 I\omega_1^2+m v_1^2.\]

The threshold occurs at \(\omega_1=0\). Thus \(\omega_{\min}=2qB/m\). Exactly at this threshold the reversed orientation is approached asymptotically. A complete reversal in finite time requires \(|\omega_0|>\omega_{\min}\). The word minimum in the source refers to this limiting threshold.
Alternative: pendulum equation
For dipole angle \(\theta\), the translational equations integrate to \(v_x=(qBd/2m)\sin\theta\), \(v_y=(qBd/2m)(1-\cos\theta)\). Substituting in the torque gives
\[\ddot\theta+\left(\frac{qB}{m}\right)^2\sin\theta=0.\]
This is the simple-pendulum equation. Reaching the inverted position needs the separatrix initial angular speed \(2qB/m\). Both signs of initial rotation have the same threshold magnitude.
d. Asymptote

nodes.alt: Original limiting trajectories of both charges, red and blue, and black centre-of-mass path approaching the vertical dashed asymptote x=D. The initial centre is at the origin and the final charge velocities point up.

children.text: At the limiting reversed orientation the angular speed tends to zero and the centre moves along \(+Y\). Generalized angular momentum about the origin is conserved:
\[L_{O,z}+B\mathbf R\cdot\mathbf p=\mathrm{const},\qquad L_{O,z}(0)=I\omega_{\min}=qBd^2.\]

On the asymptote \(x=D\), the translational angular momentum is \(2mD(qBd/m)=2qBdD\), while \(B\mathbf R\cdot\mathbf p=-BqdD\). Their sum is \(qBdD\), hence \(D=d\). Clockwise initial rotation gives asymptote \(x=-d\) and the same distance. Alternatively, on the separatrix \(\dot\theta=2(qB/m)\cos(\theta/2)\), so integrating \(dx/d\theta=(d/2)\sin(\theta/2)\) from 0 to \(\pi\) also gives \(D=d\). Original marking tables are in the PDF.

The torque is \(\boldsymbol\tau=2q\mathbf r\times(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)=-2q\mathbf B(\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf v)\), so maintaining zero rotation also requires \(\mathbf v\perp\mathbf r\). Initially the dipole points along \(X\). Thus \(\omega_0=0\), and \(\mathbf v_0\) can point along either direction of \(Y\), with arbitrary speed. Zero velocity is also a stationary limiting case.
b. Circular orbit

There is no torque because velocity is perpendicular to the rod. Centripetal balance gives \(2mv_0^2/R_c=pBv_0/R_c\). Therefore
\[\mathbf v_0=-\frac{qBd}{2m}\hat{\mathbf y},\qquad R_c=\frac{qBd}{2m|\omega_0|},\qquad (x_c,y_c)=\left(\frac{qBd}{2m\omega_0},0\right).\]

Here \(\omega_0\ne0\). Positive angular velocity places the centre on \(+X\), negative on \(-X\), while the initial velocity points downwards in both cases. The answer fields use \(w=|\omega_0|\) for radius, and signed \(\omega_0\) for \(x_c\).
c. Reversal threshold

The threshold occurs at \(\omega_1=0\). Thus \(\omega_{\min}=2qB/m\). Exactly at this threshold the reversed orientation is approached asymptotically. A complete reversal in finite time requires \(|\omega_0|>\omega_{\min}\). The word minimum in the source refers to this limiting threshold.

At the limiting reversed orientation the angular speed tends to zero and the centre moves along \(+Y\). Generalized angular momentum about the origin is conserved:
\[L_{O,z}+B\mathbf R\cdot\mathbf p=\mathrm{const},\qquad L_{O,z}(0)=I\omega_{\min}=qBd^2.\]
